brief:
WHAT HAPPENED
- Centrica's boss warned of rising energy bill payment struggles as prices are set to jump in the new year.
- US markets faced a sell-off, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones entering correction territory, partly driven by a slide in Anthropic shares.
- The UK government reached a new trade deal with the EU covering food exports, emissions, and youth schemes, sparking debate over future integration.
- President Trump threatened to ban US firms from building AI data centers overseas.
- Anthropic debuted on the stock market, becoming one of the world's most valuable public companies.

WHY IT MATTERS
- A "market correction" occurs when an index falls by at least 10% from its recent peak, often signaling investor caution.
- An "IPO" (Initial Public Offering) is the process by which a private company offers shares to the public for the first time, allowing it to raise capital.
- Energy price volatility directly impacts household disposable income, which can influence broader consumer spending and economic growth.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY
- Potential market volatility as investors react to the tech stock sell-off and Anthropic's performance.
- Further political reaction to the UK-EU trade deal and the government's plans for closer ties.
- Developments regarding the US president's proposed restrictions on overseas AI infrastructure.

IN SIMPLE TERMS
Economic uncertainty is rising as tech stocks face a rough patch and energy costs loom over household budgets. While the UK has secured a new trade deal with the EU to help the economy, the business world is focused on the high-stakes debut of AI company Anthropic. Meanwhile, US political leaders are signaling tighter control over where AI technology is built, adding another layer of complexity to the global tech landscape.
